messages.content: We have narrowed Chicago to four nights, but the dates could be June 5 to 9 or June 12 to 16. It will be me, my spouse, and our 14-year-old in one room. Can you compare River North and the South Loop without losing track of both date options?

Yes. I’ll keep both windows side by side and screen for rooms that explicitly allow three guests, then compare transit, mandatory charges, and the full four-night cost. Do you have a room setup or total budget in mind?

Two queens would be simplest. A king with a real sleeper sofa is acceptable, but not a king room where the third person is only ‘on request.’ I would like to stay near $1,600 total, though I can go somewhat higher if the location clearly earns it.

That gives me a useful cutoff. For a working comparison, I found four plausible options: the Embassy Suites Chicago Downtown River North, the Royal Sonesta Chicago Downtown, the Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown South Loop, and the Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown South Loop. The first and third have two-queen room types listed for three; the Homewood option is a king studio suite with a listed sofa bed; the Royal Sonesta needs closer room-level checking because some two-bed listings show a maximum of four while others show only two.
Drop the Royal Sonesta if the occupancy is inconsistent. What are the actual totals on the other three?

For June 5–9, the displayed figures are: Embassy Suites River North, $1,476 room and tax plus a $100 mandatory destination charge, for $1,576 total; Hilton Garden Inn South Loop, $1,248 room and tax with no mandatory property charge shown, for $1,248 total; Homewood Suites South Loop, $1,392 room and tax with no mandatory property charge shown, for $1,392 total. For June 12–16: Embassy Suites is $1,724 plus the $100 destination charge, totaling $1,824; Hilton Garden Inn is $1,436 total; Homewood Suites is $1,548 total. These are comparison-screen totals and need confirmation on the final booking page.
Does the Embassy charge get us anything useful, or is it just something added at checkout?

The listing ties it to a daily food-and-beverage credit and a few smaller benefits, but the credit has restrictions and does not reduce the amount you pay unless you use it. I would treat the full $100 as a mandatory cost, not as savings. Breakfast is included for registered guests at Embassy Suites, which is separately useful for three people.
And Homewood includes breakfast too, correct? I’m trying to understand why it costs more than the Hilton Garden Inn.

Correct. The Homewood rate includes breakfast and the studio suite has a kitchenette with a full-size refrigerator, microwave, and dishwasher. Its listed king bed plus sofa bed accommodates three. Hilton Garden Inn’s two-queen room has the more straightforward beds, but breakfast is not included in the quoted rate; adding breakfast for three each morning could narrow the difference substantially.
Location-wise, how different are they for the Field Museum, lakefront time, and a Cubs night game?

The two South Loop hotels are the strongest base for the museum portion. They are near the Roosevelt station, roughly a 20- to 25-minute walk to the Field Museum and Museum Campus, and convenient to the lakefront. For Wrigley Field, the Red Line from Roosevelt is direct and generally takes about 30 minutes on the train, plus walking and event crowds. Embassy Suites is less convenient for Museum Campus but is closer to the central River North restaurant area; the Grand Red Line stop gives you a direct ride to Addison for Wrigley, usually around 20 minutes on the train.
We will probably do two museum days and only the one baseball evening. River North restaurants are appealing, but I don’t want to pay several hundred dollars for that alone.

On that balance, South Loop is the better value and the better geographic fit. For June 5–9, Homewood saves $184 against Embassy even before assigning value to its kitchen, while Hilton Garden Inn saves $328. For June 12–16, the savings are $276 and $388 respectively. River North makes the Cubs trip somewhat easier, but not enough to offset the difference when most of the daytime plans are south of downtown.
Compare the two South Loop choices more carefully. Include the room arrangement, transit, and what we would realistically spend once breakfast is considered.

For June 5–9, Hilton Garden Inn is $1,248 with two queen beds. If breakfast averages about $18 per person after tax and tip for four mornings, that adds roughly $216, producing a practical total near $1,464. Homewood is $1,392 with one king and a sofa bed, breakfast included, so its practical total remains $1,392 unless you buy breakfast elsewhere. For June 12–16, the same comparison is about $1,652 at Hilton Garden Inn after estimated breakfasts versus $1,548 at Homewood. Both are within a short walk of Roosevelt station, so transit does not meaningfully separate them.
The sofa bed gives me pause. Does the Homewood listing definitely count our daughter in the occupancy, and are there any warnings about requesting bedding?

The selected studio suite is displayed for two adults and one child age 14, and its room description lists one king bed and one double sofa bed. I do not see ‘extra bed on request’ attached to that sleeping arrangement. Still, the final page should repeat all three guests and the sofa bed before payment. I would also ask the hotel whether bedding for the sofa bed is already in the room or needs to be requested at check-in.
What about cancellation and payment? We have not chosen the week yet, so I do not want a prepaid rate in the comparison.

The figures I used are flexible rates, not the lower prepaid offers. The current terms show no advance payment for either South Loop hotel and cancellation without penalty until 11:59 p.m. hotel local time two days before arrival. After that, the stated penalty is one night plus tax. The exact calendar deadline will differ by window: June 3 for the June 5 arrival, or June 10 for the June 12 arrival. Those terms should be verified again because hotel and third-party listings can calculate deadlines differently.
Keep both weeks open, then. Give me a short ranking for each one, and don’t pretend the breakfast estimate is a hotel charge.

For June 5–9: 1. Homewood Suites South Loop, $1,392 charged by the hotel, with breakfast included; best overall value if the confirmed sofa bed works for your daughter. 2. Hilton Garden Inn South Loop, $1,248 charged by the hotel; best bed setup and lowest fixed cost, with an optional planning estimate of about $216 for four breakfasts for three. 3. Embassy Suites River North, $1,576 including its mandatory $100 charge; best for River North dining and a somewhat easier Wrigley trip, but less aligned with the museum-heavy plan.

For June 12–16: 1. Homewood Suites, $1,548 hotel total with breakfast included. 2. Hilton Garden Inn, $1,436 hotel total, plus only whatever you independently choose to spend on breakfast. 3. Embassy Suites, $1,824 including the mandatory charge. The neighborhood ranking is unchanged, but the later window costs $156 more at Homewood, $188 more at Hilton Garden Inn, and $248 more at Embassy.
That helps. Leave airfare out until we settle the school calendar. What exactly should I confirm when I come back with the dates?

Bring back the chosen four-night window, and we can reprice the two South Loop finalists before comparing Dallas airfare. At booking, confirm that the reservation shows two adults and one child age 14; the exact room type and beds; a maximum occupancy of at least three; the four-night room-and-tax total; no mandatory destination or resort fee; payment timing; and the cancellation deadline in Chicago local time with the one-night-plus-tax penalty. For Homewood, also confirm that the sofa bed is guaranteed by the selected room description, breakfast covers all three registered guests, and sofa-bed linens are available. For Hilton Garden Inn, confirm two queen beds and keep any breakfast spending separate from the hotel total.
